newsitem.title: USA: A.M. Best downgrades Integon rating to "B+".
newsitem.headline: A.M. Best downgrades Integon rating to "B+".

text.p: A.M. Best said it lowered its rating on North Carolina-based Integon Corp Group to "B+" or very good from "A-" or excellent, after the company announced it took a $42 million reserve increase which resulted in a sizeable first quarter loss.

The insurance rating agency said the downgrade reflected the group's weakened financial condition, increased underwriting leverage, unfavourable earnings prospects and the further diminished financial flexibility of its parent holding company Integon Corp.
Integon said Monday it was reviewing all of its strategic alternatives, including a possible sale of the company.

A.M. Best said it kept a secure rating on Integon due to Integon's ability to service holding company obligation near-term. But it said the insurance company's rating was under pressure and carried a negative outlook.

"The group faces significant challenges in restoring its historical underwriting profitability while generating sufficient income and liquidity to service its substantial holding company obligations," the agency said.
A.M. Best said a strong, credible buyer could be beneficial for the insurance group's rating.

Integon's first quarter loss mostly reflected reserve deficiencies realized on its nonstandard automobile insurance policies written in 1995 and 1996 as well as unfavorable underwriting results on its 1997 business, Best said.
